feedback: If the learner thinks the reef appeared all at once, highlight the time-lapse: reefs build up slowly from countless tiny animals.
Connect the climbing species counter back to the reef-versus-bare-seabed comparison, noting that more varied structure tends to support more kinds of life.
activities.intendedInsight: Tiny living builders make a giant structure over long time; in this model a larger, more complex structure tends to offer more homes, so biodiversity tends to increase as the reef grows.
learnerActions: Seed a few polyps and watch (or step through) as they divide and secrete limestone, building structure over time.
Watch a species counter climb as the growing structure attracts more animals.
Say how this shows that tiny builders make a giant structure, and that a larger, more complex structure tends to provide homes for more kinds of animals.
activities.title: Grow a reef over time (optional dynamic model)

feedback: For a 'rock' or 'plant' answer, return to the polyp close-up and the animal-feeding evidence.
For an analogy answer based on colour, redirect to variety of life and structure-that-shelters-others.
activities.intendedInsight: Learners can state and justify all three core ideas: polyp-is-an-animal, reef biodiversity, and the analogy.
learnerActions: Answer: is coral a rock, a plant, or an animal? Justify your choice.
Compare the variety of life on a reef with that on a bare seabed and say which is more biodiverse.
Explain in a sentence why reefs are called the 'rainforests of the sea'.
activities.title: Check your understanding
